defects: On mobile, the deck overview precedes the booking lookup, pushing the crew's most frequent task down the page.
Secondary vehicle details and status annotations are small relative to the primary loading controls.
A3.note: A well-resolved operational screen that makes the actual four-lane capacity, headroom restriction, boarding priorities and local-save state visible.

defects: Supporting vehicle metadata and lane-capacity annotations are noticeably smaller than the plate and action text, making them less glanceable outdoors.
A7.note: The strongest match to the crew's job, with prominent short-plate lookup, clear loading actions, correct deck constraints and an effective navy-and-yellow hierarchy.

defects: The lane-one headroom restriction is not conspicuous in the mobile deck summary.
Small supporting labels contrast with the generous space given to the deck graphic, weakening at-a-glance operational reading.
E9.note: A clean, legible loading interface with the right capacity model, but the safety restriction and boarding-order guidance need stronger prominence.

defects: The mobile deck diagram contains very small vehicle labels and fine-grained annotations.
Queue rows are visibly cut off at the lower edge of the desktop and tablet queue panel.
The shown deck uses metres and multiple destinations rather than the required 22-unit loading model, with no conspicuous lane-one headroom warning.
J2.note: Visually competent dispatch software, but its multi-stop, metre-based loading model does not serve this ferry's simple, safety-critical boarding workflow.

defects: The mobile capture shows no usable booking search or waiting queue.
Deck labels and secondary controls become extremely small on the narrow layout.
The displayed capacity model does not communicate the required 22 units or lane-one height restriction.
N9.note: A compact desktop loading dashboard that loses the core vehicle-finding task on mobile and models the wrong vessel constraints.

defects: The fixed bottom navigation overlaps the on-screen keyboard in the desktop and tablet captures.
On mobile, the navigation bar cuts across the first booking result.
The horizontal departure strip leaves later departures outside the visible mobile area.
P4.note: A highly relevant, glove-oriented screen with short-plate entry and correct deck rules, undermined by fixed navigation obscuring the working area.

defects: The deck has six lanes and metre/weight capacities instead of the specified four lanes and 22 units.
Mobile queue text, filters and deck annotations are too small for rapid reading with a gloved outdoor workflow.
There is no conspicuous lane-one headroom warning or resident/medical boarding-priority guidance in the shown interface.
Q7.note: A coherent generic loading simulator, but its wrong deck model and dense mobile presentation make it unsuitable for this client.

defects: The six-lane, 200-metre deck contradicts the required four-lane, 22-unit vessel.
The mobile deck squeezes lane labels and vehicle markings into a small diagram.
The critical 2.1 m lane-one headroom restriction is not prominently communicated.
R2.note: Strong plate-entry and loading emphasis, including useful local-save messaging, cannot compensate for the fundamentally wrong capacity and lane model.

defects: The fixed mobile navigation cuts across a vehicle card.
Muted secondary text on the dark background has weak contrast for slipway glare.
The interface shows an upper deck, metre-based capacity and an 85-minute crossing rather than the specified vessel and 25-minute route.
R6.note: A polished-looking dark dashboard with the wrong operational assumptions and a mobile overlay that interrupts the booking list.

defects: The mobile deck compresses vehicle labels and lane markings into narrow, difficult-to-read columns.
Booking metadata and deck-capacity annotations are small for outdoor use.
The multi-destination, metre-based plan does not visibly communicate the 22-unit capacity or lane-one height restriction.
S7.note: An orderly but dense multi-stop loading planner whose information model and small operational typography miss the crew's actual needs.

defects: Loaded vehicle labels are extremely faint in the desktop-full and tablet deck views.
The fixed selected-vehicle strip covers queue and deck content in the tablet and mobile captures.
The deck reports 88 positions and lanes A-D without the required lane-one headroom warning.
W2.note: A practical-looking queue and lane picker, but low-contrast deck information and the wrong capacity model prevent safe use for this ferry.

defects: The header shows 14:25 while saying the deck closes at 14:15 'in 30 min', a contradictory operational time display.
The selected-vehicle action strip obscures queue and deck content, particularly on mobile.
The four-lane plan uses 140 metres and destination blocking rather than the required 22-unit model and headroom restriction.
Z6.note: A detailed multi-stop stowage planner, not the requested boarding tool, with an especially concerning contradiction in its departure timing.
